speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe when the lesion first appeared and if you recall any specific injury or insect bite at that site? Also, have you noticed any fever, chills, or swollen lymph nodes?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the detailed history; the ant bite and your immunocompromised state due to Crohn's disease and recent steroid use raise concern for specific infections. Has the lesion become warm, tender, or started to drain pus, and do you see any red streaks spreading up your leg? REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, CRP, and blood cultures. REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology photos of the leg lesion.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CBC with differential: WBC Normal; CRP: Not provided; Blood Cultures: Not provided; Dermatology Photos: A 4-cm tender ulcerative lesion on the anterior right leg with a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders. Pitting pedal edema is noted along with dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs. Skin Biopsy Histopathology: Neutrophilic infiltration without infection, consistent with pyoderma gangrenosum.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: ["Crohn's disease", 'Type 2 diabetes mellitus', 'Hypertension', 'Treated for anterior uveitis 8 months ago'] Social history: Recently returned from a visit to Wisconsin 2 months ago.

speaker: Patient
text: No additional systemic symptoms mentioned. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis (secondary to insect bite in an immunocompromised host).
